posts.text:
AEI’s @ben_ippolito has been appointed to the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission.

Read AEI Director of Economic Policy Studies, @MichaelRStrain, on the announcement.

aei.org/economics/ippolito-a…

The difficult part will be coming to some internal consensus about what, exactly, the United States should want other countries to do with the world’s most consequential technology, write AEI’s @audryewong and @RyanFedasiuk

warontherocks.com/cogs-of-wa…

But the AI revolution is doing what Washington lawyers and wonks couldn’t: create a new competitive environment forcing Big Tech to innovate or be usurped, writes AEI’s @JimPethokoukis

aei.org/economics/googles-ai…

The parties reward team spirit and partisan combat. Mr. Trump understands this reality. The rest of the political class is uncomfortable with it, writes AEI’s @continetti
wsj.com/opinion/free-express…

The current recycling system, however, remains inefficient. Focusing on electronic waste can change that calculation, and, in the process, take the boot of the Chinese Communist Party off the U.S. electronics industry, writes AEI's Howard Husock. washingtonexaminer.com/resto…

The noble idea behind the creation of the UN, and the privileges and immunities accorded it, have become an anachronism. Corruption, criminality, and terrorism are not rare in the world body; accountability is, write AEI’s @dpletka and @BrettDSchaefer thedispatch.com/article/unit…

Science works because it corrects course when off track. The most extreme climate scenarios have met an overdue but welcome demise, writes AEI’s @RogerPielkeJr 
washingtonpost.com/opinions/…

Just released: The American Revolution and the Constitution. In the seventh volume of the series, scholars of history, law, and politics discuss how the American Revolution unleashed the forces of constitution-making in the United States.

Purchase today: indiepubs.com/products/the-a…

We are amid a significant shift in the cultural messaging around parenthood, and we can’t throw shame or money at the problem if we hope to solve it, writes AEI’s Christine Rosen. commentary.org/articles/chri…

The Iran war is already having a dangerous impact on the Red Sea region and the Horn of Africa. It has upped the ante in an already contested area, at once increasing its importance and further polarizing the competing actors, writes AEI’s @liam_karr foreignpolicy.com/2026/05/18…

To turn things around on inflation, President Trump should turn his focus towards some of the issues that Americans have been frustrated about for decades, such as the high cost of childcare, housing, healthcare and education, writes AEI’s @MichaelRStrain ft.com/content/0a8613df-6b35…

The discipline of escalation management — of treading carefully near the nuclear brink, while making one’s adversary afraid to cross it — will be central to US policy, writes AEI’s @HalBrands aei.org/op-eds/the-age-of-nu…
